subject: Government
title: Classical and Modern Forms of Government
outline: Merits and demerits of each form

modules.title: Classical Classification of Governments
modules.html:
Aristotle classified governments by who rules and in whose interest. Each true form has a corrupt counterpart.

Number of rulersTrue form (common interest)Perverted form (self-interest)
OneMonarchyTyranny
FewAristocracyOligarchy
ManyPolity (constitutional rule)Democracy (mob rule, in Aristotle's usage)

Modern usage has reversed the last row: democracy is now the honoured term. Other classical forms include:

  • Theocracy — rule by religious leaders in the name of God (Iran, the Sokoto Caliphate).
  • Plutocracy — rule by the wealthy.
  • Gerontocracy — rule by elders, common in traditional Igbo and other African societies.
  • Anarchy — absence of government.
  • Diarchy — joint rule by two authorities, e.g. civilians and the military.

examples.q: Under Aristotle's scheme, what is the perverted form of aristocracy and why?
examples.a: Oligarchy. Aristocracy is rule by the few best in the interest of all; when those few rule for their own benefit, it degenerates into oligarchy.

modules.title: Monarchy and Autocracy
modules.html:
Monarchy is government headed by a king, queen or emir who normally holds office by hereditary right and for life.

  • Absolute monarchy — the monarch's powers are unlimited by any constitution; e.g. Saudi Arabia, or Louis XIV's France (“L'état, c'est moi”).
  • Constitutional monarchy — the monarch reigns but does not rule; real power lies with an elected prime minister and parliament; e.g. the United Kingdom, Japan, Lesotho, Morocco.

Merits of monarchy: continuity and stability, national symbol above party politics, quick decision-making in absolute form. Demerits: heredity may throw up an incompetent ruler, unaccountability, and in the absolute form, the risk of tyranny.

Autocracy / dictatorship is rule by one person whose power is unchecked and who is not accountable to the governed. Where the regime seeks to control every aspect of life — economy, education, religion, private opinion — it becomes totalitarian (Nazi Germany, Stalin's USSR). Features include a single party, censorship, a secret police, a personality cult and the suppression of opposition.

examples.q: Distinguish briefly between an absolute monarchy and a constitutional monarchy.
examples.a: In an absolute monarchy the king personally exercises unlimited governmental power. In a constitutional monarchy the king is a ceremonial head of state whose powers are defined and limited by a constitution, with real authority in an elected government.

modules.title: Democracy
modules.html:
Democracy, from the Greek demos (people) and kratos (rule), was defined by Abraham Lincoln in the Gettysburg Address (1863) as “government of the people, by the people, and for the people.”

Types:

  • Direct democracy — citizens themselves make decisions in an assembly. Practised in ancient Athens and today in some Swiss cantons, and through devices such as the referendum, initiative, plebiscite and recall.
  • Indirect or representative democracy — citizens elect representatives to act for them. Universal in modern large states, including Nigeria.

Essential conditions: universal adult suffrage; free, fair and periodic elections; multi-party competition; rule of law; independent judiciary; free press; respect for fundamental rights; an educated and tolerant electorate; and an independent electoral commission.

Merits: popular participation, accountability, protection of rights, peaceful change of government, political education. Demerits: slow decision-making, expense of elections, the risk that the majority is not always right, possible dominance of money and the manipulation of the ignorant.

examples.q: Name and explain two devices of direct democracy.
examples.a: Referendum: a proposal (often a constitutional amendment) is submitted directly to the voters for approval or rejection. Recall: voters petition to remove an elected representative before the end of the term, as provided in section 69 of Nigeria's 1999 Constitution.

modules.title: Presidential, Parliamentary, Unitary, Federal and Confederal
modules.html:
Presidential versus parliamentary systems — the standard comparison table:

BasisPresidential (Nigeria, USA)Parliamentary (UK, India)
HeadshipOne person is both Head of State and Head of Government.Separate: a ceremonial head of state and a prime minister as head of government.
Separation of powersStrict; the executive is not drawn from the legislature.Fused; ministers are members of parliament.
TenureFixed term, e.g. four years.Flexible; government falls on a vote of no confidence.
ResponsibilityPresident responsible to the electorate; removable only by impeachment.Cabinet collectively responsible to parliament.
SpeedSlower, because of checks and balances.Faster, because executive controls the legislature.

Territorial structures:

  • Unitary — all powers concentrated in one central government which may create or abolish local units; e.g. Ghana, France, Britain. Merits: cheap, uniform laws, strong centre. Demerits: remoteness, overload, unsuitable for diverse societies.
  • Federal — powers constitutionally divided between a central government and component units, each supreme in its own sphere; e.g. Nigeria, USA, India. Requires a written and rigid constitution, a supreme court to arbitrate, and a bicameral legislature.
  • Confederal — a loose union of sovereign states with a weak central body whose decisions bind states only by consent; e.g. the Senegambia Confederation (1982–1989), the USA under the Articles of Confederation.

examples.q: Give two constitutional requirements of a federal system.
examples.a: (i) A written and rigid constitution setting out the division of powers between the centre and the units. (ii) An independent supreme court empowered to interpret the constitution and settle disputes between the levels of government.

quiz.q: Aristotle's perverted form of monarchy is
quiz.solution: Rule by one in his own interest is tyranny.

quiz.q: Rule by the wealthy few is called
quiz.solution: Plutocracy is rule by the rich.

quiz.q: Government by religious leaders is
quiz.solution: Theocracy claims divine authority.

quiz.q: 'Government of the people, by the people and for the people' was said by
quiz.solution: Lincoln, Gettysburg Address, 1863.

quiz.q: A device of direct democracy is the
quiz.solution: A referendum puts a question directly to the voters.

quiz.q: In a constitutional monarchy the monarch
quiz.solution: Real power lies with the elected government.

quiz.q: A system where one person is both Head of State and Head of Government is
quiz.solution: That is the defining feature of a presidential system.

quiz.q: In a parliamentary system, ministers are
quiz.solution: Fusion of powers requires ministers to sit in parliament.

quiz.q: A government can be removed by a vote of no confidence in a
quiz.solution: The no-confidence motion is a parliamentary device.

quiz.q: Which system concentrates all powers in one central government?
quiz.solution: A unitary state has a single centre of authority.

quiz.q: A loose union of sovereign states with a weak centre is
quiz.solution: In a confederation the units retain sovereignty.

quiz.q: Which is essential to a federal system?
quiz.solution: The division of powers must be entrenched in writing.

quiz.q: Totalitarianism is characterised by
options: State control of all aspects of life
quiz.solution: Total control over society defines totalitarian rule.

quiz.q: Rule by elders is called
quiz.solution: Gerontocracy derives from the Greek for 'old man'.

quiz.q: A major demerit of democracy is that it
quiz.solution: Consultation and elections cost time and money.

quiz.q: Joint rule by civilians and the military is called
quiz.solution: Diarchy means rule by two authorities.

quiz.q: Democracy is government by:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: The People.

quiz.q: A ‘Unitary Government’ is generally best for?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Small, homogeneous countries.

quiz.q: A system of government where power is concentrated at the center is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Unitary.

quiz.q: The organ of government responsible for making laws is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Legislature.

quiz.q: A system of government where power is concentrated in the central government is called:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Unitary system.

quiz.q: The arm of government responsible for interpreting the law is the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Judiciary.

quiz.q: A coalition government is formed when:
options: No single party wins a clear majority
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: No single party wins a clear majority.

quiz.q: Which system of government concentrates power at the center?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Unitary.

quiz.q: Human rights that cannot be taken away by any government are called...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Inalienable rights.

quiz.q: Which organ of government is responsible for interpreting laws?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Judiciary.

quiz.q: A system of government where the wealthy rule is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Plutocracy.

quiz.q: The Interim National Government was headed by:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Ernest Shonekan.

quiz.q: A system of government where power is shared between the center and component units is?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Federal.

quiz.q: Which organ of government is primarily responsible for preparing the budget?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Executive.

quiz.q: Which organ of government is primarily responsible for making laws?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Legislature.

quiz.q: The ‘Vatican City’ is an example of which type of government?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Theocracy.

quiz.q: The ‘Social Contract’ theory of government was proposed by?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau.

quiz.q: A ‘Coalition Government’ occurs when?
options: Two or more parties rule together
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Two or more parties rule together.

quiz.q: Representative democracy is called:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Indirect democracy.

quiz.q: ‘Direct Democracy’ was famously practiced in?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Ancient Athens.

quiz.q: Public opinion is important in a democracy because it _____.
options: enables the government to suppress critics
serves as a guide for government policies
quiz.solution: Public opinion reflects the views of the citizenry, helping the government understand the needs and reactions of the people to its programs.

quiz.q: In a democracy, sovereignty resides in the _____.
quiz.solution: Popular sovereignty means that the ultimate power of the state belongs to the people, who exercise it through voting.

quiz.q: Federal Character Principle ensures:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Fair representation.

quiz.q: Sovereignty is located in the _____ in a democracy.
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Electorate.

quiz.q: The concept of 'Federal Character' aims to ensure:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Fair representation.

quiz.q: A direct vote by the people on a specific issue of national importance is a...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Referendum.

quiz.q: In a federal system, power is shared between:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: The Central and Component units.

quiz.q: A Unitary system concentrates power at the:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Center.

quiz.q: The principle of federal character aims at:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: Fair representation.

quiz.q: In a democracy, ultimate sovereignty belongs to?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: The People.

quiz.q: Which body is currently responsible for conducting federal elections in Nigeria?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: INEC.

quiz.q: Democracy is famously defined as rule by?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: The people.

quiz.q: ‘Collective Responsibility’ in a parliamentary system means?
options: One minister pays for everyone's mistakes
All cabinet members must support government decisions
No one is responsible for failures
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: All cabinet members must support government decisions.

quiz.q: Why did Nigeria change to a Presidential system in 1979?
options: To create a more unified, effective executive
On the advice of the UN
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: To create a more unified, effective executive.
